title.orig: I wandered lonely as a Cloud
title.en: I wandered lonely as a Cloud
title.zh: 我孤独地漫游，像一朵云

year_display.zh: 1804 年作，1807 年出版；此为 1815 年修订本

edition.en: The revised text of Poems (1815), volume I, from the scan-backed transcription on Wikisource; Wordsworth’s note on the poem omitted
edition.zh: 据维基文库依扫描本校录的《诗集》（1815）第一卷修订本；略去华兹华斯自注

basis.en: Published in 1807 and revised in 1815; the author died in 1850.
basis.zh: 1807 年出版，1815 年修订；作者卒于 1850 年。

note.en: Wordsworth’s lyric in its 1815 form, the one most people know, with the stanza “Continuous as the stars that shine” added after the first printing. It is a poem about a memory doing its work years later, the daffodils returning to “that inward eye”. Wordsworth later said the two best lines were written by his wife, Mary.
note.zh: 华兹华斯这首抒情诗的 1815 年版本，也就是大多数人熟悉的那个：初版之后，他加进了“连绵不绝，如同繁星”那一节。这是一首写记忆多年后仍在起作用的诗——水仙回到“那内在的眼睛”里。华兹华斯后来说，诗里最好的两行出自他的妻子玛丽之手。

excerpt.orig:
They flash upon that inward eye
Which is the bliss of solitude,
excerpt.en:
They flash upon that inward eye
Which is the bliss of solitude,
excerpt.zh:
它们便在那内在的眼前闪现，
那是独处时的至福，

note.en: Familiar to the point of parody, yet its last stanza states Wordsworth’s great theme, memory doing its work years later, with real grace; lovely, if lighter than his major poems.
note.zh: 熟悉到常被戏仿，末节却优雅地说出华兹华斯的大主题：记忆在多年后起作用；可爱，但比他的大作轻。
